text: Now we come to section three, and with it principle three: value without onChange freezes the box. Once again, we start with the smallest case, a box that's stuck on John. What if a box has value but no onChange? When the page opens, the box shows John, and the console already shows a red error. In Figure fifteen, the browser is at localhost five one seven three. There's one box labeled Name, and it holds John. Below it, the console has a red line. Put simply, React is complaining that we gave a form field a value without an onChange handler. In its own words, "You provided a value prop to a form field without an onChange handler. This will render a read-only field. If the field should be mutable, use default value. Otherwise, set either onChange or readOnly." And the box itself, it has value and nothing else. The file is App.jsx, and it's tiny. Line one imports useState from React. Line three starts the App component. On line four, we make a piece of state called name with its setter, setName, and it starts as John. Then the return wraps a label with the word Name in it, and inside the label sits the input on line nine. Its only prop is value equals name in curly braces. The note next to it says it plainly, "Wrong: value without onChange." Now the user clicks at the end of the box and types two letters, N and Y, to make Johnny, but the box still shows John. Figure sixteen is the same page after those two letters were typed, and honestly, it looks exactly like figure fifteen. The name box still says John, and the same red read-only error sits in the console. No line of our code removes the letters, so who removes them? React does. Here is what happens on every key in order. First, the user presses N. Second, the browser puts N into the box. Third, the box has no onChange, so no code of ours runs and name stays John. Fourth, React writes the value it was given, John, back into the box. And fifth, the box shows John again. Remember the whiteboard. A student calls out a letter, but the teacher is not listening, so the board never changes. So what the red error is telling you. React prints this error while you develop, whenever a box has value and no onChange, and it even offers three ways out. If the box should be editable, add onChange. If you only wanted a starting text, use default value instead. And if the box should really be frozen, say so with the readOnly prop. Then React knows you meant it, and the error goes away.
